description: Hello! We are a team from Kyonggi University working on "The Earth Information Jukebox." Looking for: frontend developers, data processing (Python), anyone interested in sound/music. Beginners welcome!
summary: Earth Information Jukebox is a web app that turns NASA Earth Information Center visualizations into sound in real time. As a visualization video plays, each frame is analyzed in the browser and converted into music: brightness becomes pitch, bright areas shape the tone, left/right balance moves the sound in stereo, and sudden flashes such as lightning trigger percussive hits. This addresses the challenge by making Earth science visualizations accessible to blind and low-vision users and by giving everyone a new, multi-sensory way to experience our changing planet.
details:
What it does: The app plays an EIC visualization video and generates sound from every frame in real time. Users can switch between Musical mode (pitch snapped to a pentatonic scale so it always sounds pleasant) and Raw data mode (continuous pitch that follows the data exactly), which reflects the challenge's balance between data fidelity and listenability. A "Describe what I hear" button announces the current state through screen readers, and all controls work with the keyboard.

How it works: About 10 times per second, the current frame is drawn onto a small canvas and analyzed. We calculate (1) average brightness -> pitch, (2) share of very bright pixels -> tone color and loudness, (3) left/right brightness balance -> stereo position, and (4) pixel difference from the previous frame -> percussive hit. Brightness is normalized adaptively, so dark visualizations still use the full pitch range. Sound is synthesized live with the Web Audio API; no pre-recorded audio is used.

Benefits: Makes NASA Earth data perceivable without sight, and helps all users notice patterns and sudden events they might miss visually.

Tools: HTML, JavaScript, Canvas API, Web Audio API, GitHub Pages. No external libraries.
